title: San Antonio Botanical Garden plants first 1,000 trees along Guadalupe River
text: San Antonio Botanical Garden plants first 1,000 trees along Guadalupe River WOAI NBC News Channel 4 San Antonio provides local news, weather forecasts, traffic updates, investigations, and items of interest in the community, sports and entertainment programming for San Antonio and nearby towns and communities in South Central Texas, including Windcrest, Uvalde, Universal City, Somerset, Seguin, Schertz, San Marcos,... The San Antonio Botanical Garden and community partners planted the first 1,000 native trees along the Guadalupe River in Kerr County on Thursday, part of a five-year effort to restore 50,000 trees after flooding in 2025. SAN ANTONIO - The San Antonio Botanical Garden and community partners planted the first 1,000 native trees along the Guadalupe River in Kerr County on Thursday, part of a five-year effort to restore 50,000 trees after flooding in 2025. The initiative, called TREES, or Texas Recovery for Ecological and Environmental Stability, aims to restore areas where the flood stripped native trees from the riverbank.The trees are intended to help stabilize the banks, filter water and provide habitat for wildlife.“Every tree we plant will carry a piece of what we’ve built together for generations to come,” said Katherine Trumble, the garden’s president and CEO. The Community Foundation of the Texas Hill Country has invested $3 million in the initiative through its Kerr County Flood Relief Fund. Donations to TREES will be matched dollar for dollar up to $1 million through April 15, 2027, the garden said.Since the initiative launched in August 2025, volunteers and garden staff have collected more than 850,000 native seeds from the river’s canopy — enough to grow all 50,000 trees, the garden said.
